chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had doubt in the obligatory circumambulation (tawaf), he said: 'He repeats [the tawaf] whenever he has doubt.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, if he had doubt in a voluntary circumambulation,' he said: 'He builds upon the lesser [number of circuits].'

Because this report refers to one whose doubt is in less than seven, for whenever he doubts in it, he does not have a way to complete seven circuits with certainty. And the first report is for one who has already completed and confirmed seven circuits, and he only doubts in what is added to them, so he does not pay attention to that. And there is no contradiction between the two reports.
And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for doubt during obligatory versus voluntary circumambulation (tawaf)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between doubt in obligatory (*fard*) versus voluntary (*nafl*) circumambulation, a key principle in Shia fiqh derived from Imam al-Sadiq. The text explains that for obligatory tawaf, uncertainty necessitates repetition to ensure validity, while for voluntary tawaf, one builds upon the minimum certain circuits, as perfection is not strictly required. This resolves apparent contradictions in other reports by distinguishing between doubt in the core number of circuits versus doubt in additional circuits.
